A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pregnancy is associated with a reduced risk of breast cancer, and the risk is reduced more with longer duration of gestation.
the longer the pregnancy, the lower the risk of breast cancer.
pregnancy-related protection against breast cancer is related to the duration of gestation, with the strongest protective effect after the longest pregnancies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women who have a pregnancy of less than 32 completed weeks of gestation have a significantly increased risk for developing breast cancer.
the length of gestation has a protective effect on the risk of developing breast cancer.
the risk reduction from a pregnancy is not uniform across all women.
